summary: Leaves the run with one sourced, unexecuted lead rather than closing on an unsupported claim. Reading the follower's prepare handler shows a second place where a prefix below the compacted index can be asked of the storage, this time by the replica itself: when the follower's accepted round exceeds the leader's reported one it answers with create_log_sync(prep.decided_idx, prep.decided_idx), and when the rounds are equal and its accepted index is greater it answers with create_log_sync(prep.accepted_idx, prep.decided_idx), so both numbers come from the new leader's Prepare and are used as the common prefix into the follower's own storage. For an entry type whose Snapshot is NoSnapshot that prefix reaches get_suffix, whose subtraction of the trimmed index is unguarded, so a follower whose compacted index lies above the number its new leader reports would abort inside its own message handling, while the snapshot-capable type takes the Complete-snapshot branch instead - which is why the probe must run both entry types. Reachability needs a legal history in which a newly elected leader missed a decision the follower learned, and the existing harness can produce that by cutting the future leader off while the older leader decides and then electing it, so the lead is cheap to test rather than a new fixture. Recorded as a new question on the drift investigation - with the hypothesis, the cited handler, storage and snapshot material, and a discriminator naming the decisive observation and the reachability step - and as a knowledge entry for the handler branch itself, both clearly marked as sourced expectations rather than observations. Nothing else changed: every other account, gap and discriminator keeps its current conclusion and limits, and no execution was requested, so the remaining work is explicitly a probe someone can pick up rather than an unresolved claim.
